segments: The Chronography: Kings. {OCR?} In the year
1531 of the Greeks [1220 AD],
in the Latter Kanun [January]:
Sultan Izz al-Din Kaykaus, son of Kaykhusraw, son of Qilij Arslan, the ruler of the house of the Romans [Rūm], died.
For he had gathered armies to go again to wage war with al-Ashraf in Mesopotamia;
and when he reached Melitene, the disease of phthisis worsened upon him,
and therefore he turned back from it and died.
And the grandees sent and brought out Ala al-Din Kayqubad, who was imprisoned in the fortress of Masara on the Blessed Mountain,
and made him king over them.
And some were saying
that Sultan Izz al-Din himself, before he died, sent and released him from prison and made the grandees swear allegiance in his presence,
because he had no son who was fit for the kingdom.
Now that Sultan Ala al-Din Kayqubad,
who at the beginning of his reign, when he saw that his enemies were numerous—
namely the Greeks and the Armenians around him, and also his uncle, the ruler of Erzurum—
made friendship with Malik al-Ashraf, and asked that his sister be given to him as a wife;
who was indeed given to him after three years.
And in this same year,
which is the year six hundred and sixty-eight of the Armenians [1219-1220 AD],
died Leo, king of Cilicia,
a warlike man in battles and victorious in combats.
And he had only a daughter,
whose name was Zabel [Isabella].
And Sir Danvali [Adam of Gaston {OCR?}] , the lord of the fortresses of the seacoast, took over the administration of the king's daughter and of the kingdom for about two years,
until the Ismailites [Assassins] killed him.
And in the year 617
617 of the Arabs [1220 AD], in the first month [Muharram]:
Genghis
Khan went in person and encamped against the city of Bukhara,
which was the dome of the faith of the Muslims in all the regions beyond the Gihon [Oxus].
Now he encamped at the gate {OCR?} of the fortress;
and there also came numerous legions of the Mongols,
who exceeded the number of locusts and ants,
and troop by troop they encamped around the wretched city.
Now there were in it about twenty thousand horsemen,
and famous commanders: Sevinch Khan and Keshli Khan
and... {OCR?}
